findings.evidence: PeterWeyl.lean:487-494 proof is `rw [coe_peterWeylBasis, peterWeylFamily_apply, ContRepresentation.matrixCoeffLp_def, map_smul]`; `peterWeylFamily` (line 374) is already defined as `(√dim : 𝕜) • matrixCoeffLp ...` and `matrixCoeffLp_def` (MatrixCoefficient.lean:79) is `rfl`; MatrixCoefficient.lean:94-121 provide the `matrixCoeffLp_{zero,add,smul}_*` simp lemmas stated on the wrapper.
findings.fix: Drop both lemmas once `coeFn_peterWeylFamily` exists; if a pointwise statement is still wanted, state it as `peterWeylBasis h x = (√dim : 𝕜) • ContRepresentation.matrixCoeffLp ...` keeping the wrapper intact.
findings.issue: `peterWeylBasis_apply` (and its clone `stdPeterWeylBasis_apply`, line 663) is the composite of three existing lemmas (`coe_peterWeylBasis`, `peterWeylFamily_apply`, `matrixCoeffLp_def`) and its only purpose is to feed the inline a.e. argument above. As exported API it also unfolds the `matrixCoeffLp` wrapper, pushing `ContinuousMap.toLp` out through the `√dim •` scalar, so downstream goals no longer match the `matrixCoeffLp_*` simp set.

summary: The proofs are short and free of `change`/`show` or brittle rewrite chains, but the a.e.-representative fact for a Peter-Weyl basis element is derived inline inside `peterWeylBasis_repr_apply` instead of being factored out, and it bypasses the existing `ContRepresentation.coeFn_matrixCoeffLp`. The two `*_apply` lemmas exist only to support that inline detour and unfold the `matrixCoeffLp` wrapper.
